current_example.title: Example: Maximums and Minimums in More Complex Settings

q-181990.name: Question 1
q-181990.worked_solution:
Recall that 

- ${x}_{max}$ is the maximum of a set $S$ if ${x}_{max}\in S$ and $x\le {x}_{max}$ for all $x\in S,$ and

- ${x}_{min}$ is the minimum of a set $S$ if ${x}_{min}\in S$ and ${x}_{min}\le x$ for all $x\in S.$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}min(B) & =min\{9,\,3,\,0,\,7\}=0 \\ max(B) & =max\{9,\,3,\,0,\,7\}=9\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 0
9

EXPLANATION

Recall that

  • xmax is the maximum of a set S if xmax∈S and x≤xmax for all x∈S, and

  • xmin is the minimum of a set S if xmin∈S and xmin≤x for all x∈S.

Therefore, we have the following:

min(B)=min{9,3,0,7}=0max(B)=max{9,3,0,7}=9

q-182012.name: Question 6
q-182012.problem:
Complete the following reasoning about the set $S=(-3,\infty ):$

The value $20$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because {{field-1}} and yet {{field-2}}.
q-182012.worked_solution:
Recall that ${x}_{max}$ is the maximum of a set $S$ if 

- ${x}_{max}\in S,$ and

- $x\le {x}_{max}$ for all $x\in S.$

In our case, the value $20$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because, for example, $21\in S$ and yet $21>20.$

q-182005.name: Question 7
q-182005.problem:
Complete the following reasoning about the set $S=(-\infty ,-2):$

The value $-2$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because {{field-1}}.
q-182005.worked_solution:
Recall that ${x}_{max}$ is the maximum of a set $S$ if 

- ${x}_{max}\in S,$ and

- $x\le {x}_{max}$ for all $x\in S.$

In our case, the value $-2$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because $-2\notin S.$

q-182005.html:
Question 7
?
Complete the following reasoning about the set S=(−∞,−2):

The value −2 is not the maximum of the set S because
−3≤−2
−3≤−2
−2∉S
−2<∞
−2∈S
−1≥−2
−1∉S
.
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that xmax is the maximum of a set S if

  • xmax∈S, and

  • x≤xmax for all x∈S.

In our case, the value −2 is not the maximum of the set S because −2∉S.
q-182005.knowledge_point: Explaining the Existence of a Maximum or Minimum

q-181729.name: Question 8
q-181729.problem:
Complete the following reasoning about the set $S=(-\infty ,1):$

The value $1$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because {{field-1}}.
q-181729.worked_solution:
Recall that ${x}_{max}$ is the maximum of a set $S$ if 

- ${x}_{max}\in S,$ and

- $x\le {x}_{max}$ for all $x\in S.$

In our case, the value $1$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because $1\notin S.$

q-182000.html:
Question 9
?
Complete the following reasoning about the set S=(−∞,−3]:

The value −3 is the
minimum
minimum
maximum
of the set S because
−3∈S
−3∉S
−3∈S
and
x≤−3
x≤−3
x≥−3
for all x∈S.
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that xmax is the maximum of a set S if

  • xmax∈S, and

  • x≤xmax for all x∈S.

In our case, we have that −3 is the maximum of the set S because

  • −3∈S, and

  • x≤−3 for all x∈S.

q-182010.name: Question 10
q-182010.problem:
Complete the following reasoning about the set $S=(4,\infty ):$

The value $100$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because {{field-1}} and yet {{field-2}}.
q-182010.worked_solution:
Recall that ${x}_{max}$ is the maximum of a set $S$ if 

- ${x}_{max}\in S,$ and

- $x\le {x}_{max}$ for all $x\in S.$

In our case, the value $100$ is not the maximum of the set $S$ because, for example, $101\in S$ and yet $101>100.$
